text:
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] kv-cache fission burst — elevated tail latency and 5xx for continuous-batching on kv-tier-2. Auto-pager @sophia is triggered. model_family: Llama-MQA, Qwen-MQA; region: us-west1; started ~now :rotating_light:

ops-bot: Metrics snapshot: P95 token latency up 4x, batch rejection rate 18%, kv-evictions spiking. Logs show repeated KV_LOOKUP timeouts and large prefix cardinality samples.

sophia: acknowledging, I'm oncall. jumping in. can someone post the quick mitigation checklist? :point_down:

anya: quick notes — looks like continuous-batch window collapsed after a sudden prefix-cardinality spike from a few noisy customers. KV cache grew and triggered aggressive eviction -> cache churn -> more misses -> higher batch sizes -> perf cliff. suspect MQA routines exacerbating prefix fanout.

matt: confirmed on runtime traces. mqa paths (kv_prefetch + cont_batch) are creating oversized batches for sequences with many short prefixes. stacktrace snippets show the runtime stalling on kernel selection under load.

liz: customer-impact: Support reports two customers saw latencies > 10s for chat endpoints and one tenant hit degraded throughput. No data plane errors beyond 5xx for generation endpoints. prepping customer comms.

sam: immediate mitigation idea: 1) force cont-batch-size cap to 8 for affected pools, 2) increase kv-eviction-threshold to reduce churn, 3) route traffic for Llama-MQA -> Llama-GQA variant for heavy prefixes.

matt: I can push a hotfix to batch config. deploying a conservative cap using runtime flag:
```bash
# deploy to kv-tier-2 pools
redwoodctl runtime set-flag --pool kv-tier-2 --flag cont_batch.max_tokens=8 --reason "mitigate cache-fission burst"
```

matt: doing canary to 3 shards now. will monitor p95 and eviction rate.

anya: also recommend disabling aggressive kv-prefetch for MQA models in that pool until we diagnose. flag: kv.prefetch.enabled=false for model_selector:mqa.*

deploy-bot: build/9876 -> runtime-config applied to shard-17, shard-42, shard-101 (canary).

sophia: can someone validate a rollback plan in case the hotfix regresses? steps + who?

matt: rollback is simple: revert flag via redwoodctl and scale cont-batch back to default. i'll own rollback. notification channel: #eng-runtime. ETA 2m for canary metrics.

liz: I'll open a blame-free incident update for affected customers and add the initial impact notes. tagging CS to prepare holding template.

sam: telemetry query I ran shows large prefix-cardinality coming from two customer API keys — isolating for rate-limiting. recommending temporary per-key token quota lower to limit blast radius.

anya: follow-up diagnostic commands:
```sql
SELECT prefix, count(*) as hits FROM kv_access_logs WHERE time > now()-10m GROUP BY prefix ORDER BY hits DESC LIMIT 20;
```
results show top prefixes are chat-session tokens + some malformed bot traffic.

matt: can confirm canary dropped P95 from 2.1s -> 650ms on canary shards; eviction rate down 60%. promoting to 30% traffic in 10m.

sophia: handing off to night oncall @sam in 20m. please capture runbook steps and escalation targets.

sam: ack, I'll take over monitoring. plan for next 30m: 1) promote hotfix to all kv-tier-2, 2) apply per-key throttles for noisy keys, 3) start a deeper postmortem focusing on MQA prefetch heuristics.

matt: promotion started. patch id: cfg-2026-3460001111-hotfix.

deploy-bot: promotion complete to all kv-tier-2 pools.

anya: next actions for postmortem: collect model-specific KV hit/miss by prefix, verify MQA greedy prefetch behavior, simulate high-cardinality prefix load for Llama vs Mistral vs Qwen to compare.

liz: customer update draft: "We've identified a cache/continuous-batching interaction affecting certain workloads (not all customers). We applied an emergency batch-size cap and reduced cache churn; latency is returning to normal for the majority of traffic. We're investigating the root cause and will follow up with a timeline." sending to CS for review.

sophia: handoff note for @sam: watch for re-emergence near midnight UTC, alert if P95 rises >1s above baseline or if 5xx rate >0.5% for generation endpoints. if that happens, escalate to @matt and @anya immediately.

sam: acknowledged. adding runbook link and all artifacts to the incident ticket.

ops-bot: Incident 3460001111 marked as mitigated — regression mitigated by cfg-2026-3460001111-hotfix. Follow-up: postmortem + model testing scheduled.

sophia: closing handoff. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
